summary.title: Article: Product vs Feature Teams
summary.one_liner: Learn the difference between empowered product teams, which own outcomes and value risk, and feature teams, which deliver roadmap output, and why the product manager role differs in each.
keywords: how to tell if my team is a feature team
takeaways: Empowered product teams are cross-functional (product, design, engineering), measured by outcomes rather than output, and free to choose how to solve problems.
On a feature team, value and business viability sit with the stakeholder who requested the feature, while the product manager often becomes a project manager.
In an empowered team, the product manager owns value and viability, the designer owns usability, and the tech lead owns feasibility.
The article lists diagnostic questions, such as whether you receive roadmaps with dates or problems with outcomes, to tell which model your team follows.
summary.summary: Marty Cagan's essay argues that many teams labeled 'product teams' are actually feature teams focused on output from a roadmap, and that delivery teams (scrum/SAFe style) are re-packaged waterfall. He defines empowered product teams by cross-functional makeup, outcome measurement, and autonomy, then compares the product manager's responsibilities in each model across the four risks: value, usability, feasibility, and viability. The piece closes with a checklist of indicators for diagnosing your team's model and a call to evaluate product advice by which model it assumes.
